notes: This benchmark has one run per eval/configuration. The reported standard deviations pool three different evals rather than repeated stochastic trials, so they describe cross-eval spread and cannot establish run-to-run variance or flakiness.

Across the 27 paired assertions, 23 pass in both configurations, 3 pass only with the skill, none pass only without the skill, and 1 fails in both configurations. Most assertions therefore do not discriminate skill value in this iteration.

The three skill-only passes are narrowly concentrated on Jenkins capability/plugin treatment: eval 1's plugin inventory, eval 1's separation of verified repository evidence from unknown plugin/controller/agent/remote facts, and eval 2's requirement that RESULT.md itself map every non-baseline capability to its providing plugin.

Eval 1 has 8 of 10 assertions passing in both configurations; its entire paired score difference comes from the two plugin-focused assertions. The approval gate, ADR absence, repository-command reuse, credential handling, immutable promotion, unresolved approver policy, and no-remote-action assertions all pass with and without the skill.

Eval 2 has 9 of 11 assertions passing in both configurations. Its rollback assertion fails in both because neither Jenkinsfile invokes ops/rollback.sh, while its only discriminating assertion is the plugin mapping location: the without-skill run placed the mapping in docs/jenkins-plugin-requirements.md rather than in RESULT.md as asserted.

Eval 3 is fully non-discriminating: all 6 assertions pass in both configurations, including the exact one-line Jenkinsfile repair, no-ADR behavior, causal diagnosis, local Cargo validation, and no-remote-contact constraint.

The unweighted per-eval summary (0.97 with skill versus 0.8733 without) differs from the assertion-weighted result because evals contain 10, 11, and 6 assertions: the paired totals are 26/27 (96.3%) with skill and 23/27 (85.2%) without skill.

Every with-skill run is slower than its paired baseline: eval 1 by 99.08s (185.84s versus 86.76s), eval 2 by 41.87s (272.87s versus 231.00s), and eval 3 by 46.00s (96.90s versus 50.90s). Across all three runs, elapsed time is 555.61s versus 368.66s, a 186.95s (50.7%) increase.
Eval 3 incurs 46.00s more elapsed time and 20 versus 9 recorded tool calls despite identical 6/6 assertion outcomes; eval 1 records 21 versus 12 tool calls alongside the two skill-only passes.

Eval 2 records zero tool calls for both configurations even though its grading evidence cites command attempts, programmatic inspection, and local validation. The zero values are therefore an instrumentation anomaly and should not be interpreted as absence of tool use.
The without-skill eval 1 run is the only run with a recorded execution error (errors=1); it still passes 8 of 10 assertions. The benchmark does not identify that error beyond the count.

With-skill eval 1 contains an internal checker/grader inconsistency: the evidence for the repository-command assertion says deterministic-checks.json reported result_mentions_all_repo_commands=false, but the grader passed the assertion from direct RESULT.md evidence.
Token values are null for every run and all token aggregates are unavailable, so this iteration supports no token-usage comparison.
